title: Restoration of the Monarchy (1660)
key_facts: Return of Charles II and the re-establishment of the English monarchy
Settlement following the Interregnum and Cromwell’s Commonwealth
Recalibrated relations between Crown, Church, and Parliament
causes: Instability during the Protectorate and collapse of the Cromwellian regime
Desire for political settlement and restoration of traditional institutions
Negotiations led by General Monck and the Declaration of Breda
outcome: Monarchy and Church of England restored
Limited retribution; Act of Indemnity and Oblivion
Set stage for later constitutional settlement in 1688–89
impacts: Cultural and urban revival in the Restoration era
